title: rework-ci-cache-keying-and-pin-action-shas-to-reduce-flaky-builds
author: Priya Chandrasekaran
description: Motivation: CI cache misses and transient action version updates have been the dominant source of CI flakiness and increased build times. This PR introduces a robust cache keying strategy across language ecosystems, pins critical GitHub Actions to SHAs, normalizes the dependency install paths to reduce cache fragmentation, and removes legacy/unused workflows. Summary of changes: 1) Introduced a deterministic, multilayer cache key format: scope|os|lang|dep-hash|tool-versions. The format reduces false invalidation by separating OS/runtime changes from dependency changes. 2) Centralized cache key generation in .github/actions/ci-utils with a small composite action that exposes an output CACHE_KEY and RESTORE_KEY so all workflows share identical key derivation. 3) Pinned top-level actions (actions/checkout, actions/cache, actions/setup-node, actions/setup-java) to specific SHAs and added a small helper script (scripts/refresh-action-shas.py) to refresh SHAs in a controlled PR with audit notes. 4) Migrated Node pipelines to use workspace-level lockfile hashing (package-lock.json + pnpm-lock.yaml detection) and a normalized node_modules path to allow consistent caches across matrix axes. 5) Replace ad-hoc caching in Python and Go jobs with the shared composite action and explicit pip/pipx wheel cache layering, including a requirements.txt hash and venv path normalization. 6) Trimmed redundant matrix axes: we now avoid running full integration on both ubuntu-20 and ubuntu-22 unless OS-specific tests are impacted; integration runs pick ubuntu-22 by default. 7) Removed three legacy CI workflows (ci/legacy-*-pipeline.yml) and added a migration doc under docs/ci/cache-keying.md describing how to adopt the new cache keys locally. Rollout plan and safety: changes were introduced behind flags in affected workflows and validated across the repo using a small canary: redwood-examples and redwood-sdk-python. We ran 10 consecutive CI runs on the canary branches to measure cache hit rates and observed a median cache miss reduction from 38% to 7% and average pipeline time drop of ~22%. The actions SHAs are recorded in .github/actions/manifest.txt for auditability and will be rotated by the tooling in a separate follow-up PR. Testing and verification: unit tests for the composite action and the sha-refresh script were added; all existing lint/test/integration suites were executed on the branch; performance sampling used existing perf-canary infra. Migration notes for integrators: if you have custom caching code, migrate to the ci-utils composite action and remove ad-hoc restoration logic. For self-hosted runners, ensure the normalized cache paths exist or disable sharing via an env flag. Follow-ups: (a) automated periodic PRs from the sha-refresh bot to keep action SHAs up to date, (b) add an opt-in 'ci-fast' pipeline for quick pre-commit checks, (c) add observability metrics for cache-hit vs miss per repo, and (d) evaluate switching to the new actions/cache v4 when available. Related: ENG-3012 addresses flaky pipeline noise; SUP-4721 is the customer incident that surfaced the worst cache scenarios. Checklists: - [x] Implement deterministic cache key generation - [x] Add composite action and tests - [x] Pin critical actions to SHAs and add refresh tooling - [x] Migrate node/python/go jobs to use shared composite - [x] Update docs and deprecate legacy workflows - [x] Run canary and collect hit-rate metrics - [x] Get approvals from infra and platform reviewers
commits: ci: add composite cache key action and tests
ci: pin actions/checkout and actions/cache to SHAs
scripts: add refresh-action-shas.py with dry-run mode
ci(pipelines): normalize node install paths and lockfile hashing
ci: migrate python/go jobs to composite cache action
ci: remove legacy workflows and add docs entry
review_conversation: Marta Lopez: This looks promising, but can we avoid pinning everything forever? Suggest recording SHAs and tooling to refresh with audit comments.
Priya Chandrasekaran: Agreed; added scripts/refresh-action-shas.py and manifest.txt; refresh is a separate PR generated by the bot per rollout plan.
Derek Nguyen: I'm concerned about matrix reduction removing coverage for ubuntu-20. Please ensure a weekly compat job remains.
Priya Chandrasekaran: Added a weekly compat workflow and documented it in docs/ci/cache-keying.md.
Samir Patel: Small nit: venv path normalization might break some legacy dev scripts in infra. Can you add a toggle env var?
Priya Chandrasekaran: Added CI_CACHE_NORMALIZE=false env override and noted migration steps in the docs.
Marta Lopez: CI runs flaked on the first attempt due to a race in cache writes; observed better stability after switching to upload-only-on-miss semantics.
Priya Chandrasekaran: Fixed: composite action now sets upload-on-miss and gate to avoid parallel writes. Verified in canary runs.
release_notes: Improved CI caching and stability: deterministic cache keys, pinned GH Actions to SHAs with refresh tooling, normalized dependency cache paths, removed legacy workflows, and trimmed CI matrix to reduce redundant runs. Expected outcome: fewer flaky runs, faster pipelines, and clearer auditability for action versions. Follow-ups: periodic SHA refresh PRs and cache hit telemetry.
